purpose: R CRAN million-row query growth and index-plan verification

environment.host: Intel Core i9-9880H, 64 GiB RAM, macOS 14.7.8 x86_64

notes: The two extra suite/snapshot rows are the live r-hosted and r-group repository state.
The one extra pending suite and observed expired leases are live publication state outside the synthetic fixture.
Package and path hashes are fixed-width sequential synthetic values; selectivity and index shape match production SHA-256 columns.

method.cache_state: warmed execution after fixture load and ANALYZE or VACUUM ANALYZE
method.scope: database executor time; excludes JDBC mapping, network transfer, index serialization, and blob access

mysql.access: unique hash lookup plus full-path collision check
two bounded index ranges for the MySQL keyset predicate
reverse index lookup over 100 package versions
100 relation matches and 100 package point probes
bounded pending range and 101 repository point probes

mysql.index: idx_r_snapshot_cleanup plus idx_r_snapshot_retention plus suite primary key
mysql.access: 256 cleanup rows; exactly 3 retention rows and 1 suite row probed per candidate
unique point lookup plus full-path collision check

postgresql.access: index hash lookup plus full-path collision check
ordered index lookup over 100 package versions
100 relation matches and 100 package point probes
bounded pending bitmap range and two memoized repository point probes
256 cleanup rows; exactly 3 retention rows and 1 suite row probed per candidate
index point lookup plus full-path collision check
bounded primary-key range with zero rows removed by the snapshot filter

remediation.finding: The first MySQL snapshot-retention shape could scan progressively older revisions because EXISTS discarded the requested ordering.
remediation.before: The first 256-row batch examined an average of 132 newer rows per candidate and took 28.7 ms; later batches could grow with candidate revision.
remediation.change: Store an indexed publish-complete discriminator and compare candidates with the Nth-newest indexed revision waterline.
remediation.after: Both engines examine exactly three retention rows per candidate; MySQL took 8.29 ms and PostgreSQL took 5.191 ms for 256 candidates.
